title: Hi-Hi

source.quote: The participants in a ritual will often keep a close count of the strokes exchanged.

setting: Monday morning. Mr. C is back after two weeks away. He's standing by the coffee machine, and the whole floor can see he's waiting to be noticed.

L1.line: Dev walks past Mr. C, says "Hey" without stopping, and keeps walking to his desk.
L1.question: Mr. C's shoulders drop and he turns back to his coffee. What went wrong with Dev's greeting, in stroke terms?

options.text: Nothing - "Hey" is a complete ritual greeting.
options.feedback: A one-word "Hey" pays what a daily passing nod costs. Mr. C has been gone two weeks and is owed a bigger ritual than that.

options.text: Dev under-paid the ritual - two weeks away earns more than a one-word, no-stop "Hey."
options.feedback: Right. Rituals are precise stroke exchanges, not empty noise - the length and attention of a greeting has to scale with what it's actually marking.

options.text: Dev should have asked Mr. C a real question about the trip - this isn't about strokes at all.
options.feedback: That might help, but it's not what diagnosed the failure - the failure here is specifically a stroke shortfall, not a lack of curiosity.

L1.lesson: Rituals participants keep a close count of the strokes exchanged - picture holding out a hand for a handshake and having it ignored. A returning-from-vacation greeting carries an implicit price; paying less than that price registers as a snub even though nobody ever states the price out loud.

L2.intro: Your turn. Mr. C is still standing at the coffee machine. Two weeks of silence doesn't get paid off with a nod.

cues: lingering, not walking away - leaving room for more

options.text: "Hey, welcome back! Two weeks, right? How was it - good to be back, or already missing the beach?"
options.outcome: Mr. C's whole posture changes - he turns fully toward Troy. "Honestly, both," he says, and tells him about the flight delay while they wait for the coffee.
options.lesson: A greeting that's specific (names the two weeks), asks a real question, and leaves room for an answer pays roughly what's owed - enough to register as a genuine welcome, not so much it reads as performance.

options.outcome: Mr. C's smile drops half a notch. He turns back to the coffee machine and doesn't bring it up again - but mentions to Priya later that "nobody even asked."
options.lesson: Under-paying a scaled-up ritual doesn't just feel rude in the moment - an unmet stroke-hunger here doesn't vanish, it gets carried to the next person, or quietly banked as a small resentment.

options.text: "Oh my gosh, welcome back!! Tell me literally everything - the flight, the hotel, the food, ALL of it, I have so many questions!"
options.outcome: Mr. C laughs, a little thrown. "Whoa - okay! Let me get my coffee first." It lands as enthusiasm, slightly too much of it, delivered in the doorway while three people wait behind Troy for the machine.
options.lesson: Over-paying isn't dishonest the way a discount is, but a ritual that balloons past its slot stops feeling like a ritual and starts feeling like a pitch - the stereotyped, proportionate exchange is exactly what makes a ritual comfortable instead of overwhelming.

options.text: Avoid eye contact and grab your coffee quickly, hoping someone else greets him first.
options.outcome: Someone else does greet him, enthusiastically. Mr. C beams at them and barely registers that Troy was in the room. Later, Troy feels oddly resentful that he didn't get credit for being friendly.
options.lesson: Ducking the exchange entirely while quietly keeping score on who gets social credit for it isn't a neutral non-choice - it's a small setup for exactly the kind of resentment that fuels bigger games later.

fields.label: Draw the vectors for a standard ritual greeting, and for Troy's best (matched) greeting.
In under 50 words: why does TA Today say ritual participants 'keep a close count' of strokes, and what does that explain about why Dev's one-word "Hey" landed as a snub?

echo.setting: A week later: a friend texts back after being unreachable for ten days.
echo.line: hey!! sorry, insane week, miss u
echo.shape: same counter mechanic - how much greeting does ten days of silence cost now?
